answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock 100 tokens for 30 days before it can bid on jobs, and caps concurrent bids per bonded identity. Agents named nectar, saffron, and falcon face the same rule as every newcomer. An attacker creating 1,000 identities must therefore immobilize 100,000 tokens for a month. Extra names remain possible, but they cannot expand bidding capacity without proportional capital and its opportunity cost.
